summary: Fresh tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz and US yields above 5% weigh on Monday's setup, with steady foreign buying and an oil market worried about surplus the main offsets.

detail.leaders: Upstream oil producers if crude jumps on the Hormuz news; large caps that foreign buyers have favoured
detail.laggards: Oil-marketing companies and airlines if crude rises; IT and rate-sensitives while US yields stay above 5%
detail.tone: A look-ahead to Monday 16 November. The evening's change is in the Gulf: Iran says more tankers hit mines in Hormuz on Saturday, a risk Brent has not yet priced since it last traded on Friday.
watch: How crude opens on Monday after the weekend tanker strikes
Whether foreign buying holds up with US yields above 5% and the rupee weak
October wholesale inflation, due on Monday

top.title: More tankers hit mines in Hormuz
top.line: Iran says tankers struck mines on Saturday; one live tally puts it at five in 24 hours
more: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say the ships used unauthorised routes; the claims are unverified
Iran also says it shot down a US drone over Qeshm Island
Brent last settled flat at $95.84 on Friday, before Saturday's reports

top.line: Treasury yields rose on Friday after hot US inflation data and hawkish Fed remarks
more: Reports put Friday's 10-year yield between about 5.11% and 5.15%
One report says it rose about 30 basis points over the week
The dollar index is near a 19-month high

top.line: The government is scheduled to release October WPI data on November 16
